pr_comments:
> One thing I see as slightly odd is that with fromdata you have to call fromdata_init first. But not with todata. That's probably correct behaviour but the asymmetry seems strange.

Let's not bend over backwards over such things...

> Let's not bend over backwards over such things...

:(  Consistency to developers matters a great deal.

> :( Consistency to developers matters a great deal.

I think the problem here is "consistency with what"? "fromdata" is essentially very similar to a keygen operation and the "init then generate" pattern is consistent with how normal keygen works. "todata" is not a keygen operation and the "init then generate" pattern doesn't make a lot of sense and there seems no need for "todata" to attempt to be consistent with keygen. This is where I think the inconsistency comes from - in spite of the apparent similarity in names they are different types of function.
This looks ok to me, but I guess we need to wait for #14785 to be merged.

issue_context.title: Should there be an EVP_PKEY_todata()?
issue_context.body: We have the API `EVP_PKEY_fromdata()` which creates a new key based on a set of OSSL_PARAMs. It is possible to get param data from an existing key using `EVP_PKEY_get_params`. However this requires you to know up front all the params data that you might want to get and to set up the OSSL_PARAM array accordingly. It would be nice to have an `EVP_PKEY_todata()` function which creates an OSSL_PARAM array for you and populates it with all the relevant parameters required for a subsequent `EVP_PKEY_fromdata()` call to be successful.
comments:
Why not use the output from the `EVP_PKEY_gettable_params` call to get the params?
The gettable params would need to be cloned to avoid them being read only.
Are all required parameters (sufficient to re-create the key using `EVP_PKEY_fromdata()`) exposed by `EVP_PKEY_gettable_params`?

> Are all required parameters (sufficient to re-create the key using `EVP_PKEY_fromdata()`) exposed by `EVP_PKEY_gettable_params`?

I'd consider that to be a bug in the provider if they aren't.

There is however a problem with usability of the simple "cloning" - for bignum parameters you do not know how big the data will be in advance and you'll have to call the getparams twice with preallocations. This is clearly visible in the EVP_PKEY_get_bn_param() implementation.
The internal export function passes a callback, which is passed an OSSL_PARAM array constructed by the provider. Just wrap that with a public API, where the callback comes from the caller. Done deal.

I think it would be more user/application friendly, to clone the OSSL_PARAM array for the user -- gets the memory allocated on the proper side of the provider boundary, lets the app take control of the life time etc.
I think that duplicating the OSSL_PARAM array should be a decision for the caller (user/application), not a unilateral decision that we make for them.

You need to look at what the export does before making this comment.
By the time the export has finished the params returned from the  callback are destroyed. This is great if you are called import in the callback.. It is not so great if you want the params to hang around after the call.
I agree with @slontis here.  We need persistence,

> You need to look at what the export does before making this comment.

I'm fully aware how it works.

> By the time the export has finished the params returned from the callback are destroyed.

The params *recieved by* the callback only exist until the callback ends, yes.  And?
Could there be a misunderstanding here?  When I said that we could simply make the currently internal export function (`evp_keymgmt_util_export()`) public, I really meant that, and that means that the application would provide the callback.  Therefore, it would be entirely up to the application what they want to do with the params that the callback receives.

In other words, I was seeing this:

``` C
int EVP_PKEY_todata(const EVP_PKEY *pk, int selection,
                    OSSL_CALLBACK *export_cb, void *export_cbarg);
```

But, from seeing discussions here and in #14785, it looks like we have very different ideas of what `EVP_PKEY_todata()` should offer.  Would you mind showing your idea in a bit more concrete form?

> I'm fully aware how it works.

What you have above is fine.. I want the param data to be available **AFTER** EVP_PKEY_todata() has been called. i.e within the export_cb the user can use the OSSL_PARAM_dup() **if the user wants to.**

OR if we wanted to not expose the callback at all to the user..
````
int EVP_PKEY_todata(const EVP_PKEY *pk, int selection, OSSL_PARAM **params)
````
and then have a fixed callback that uses the dup..

So no the ideas are not really different.. I think returning the OSSL_PARAM the second way is more user friendly..

@levitte that is a pretty poor interface compared to the fromdata (other side).
That interface existing doesn't hurt to have (and exposed) - but we should be able to offer a simple interface that returns a usable OSSL_PARAM array and expect our users to actually use that interface in preference to having to run an iterator and arrange collection themselves.
I'm fine with both.  We could expose `evp_pkey_util_export()` as `EVP_PKEY_export()` if that makes everyone feel better.
A callback is a dreadful API for this.  An OSSL_PARAM array is what we accept as input, we should be able to output one.  It is much friendlier and easier to use.

I would still like to offer the *choice* to the user / application.  We do not know what the resulting OSSL_PARAM will be used for, but you can be sure that there are some who'd prefer not to waste more memory allocation and copying than necessary.

Can we settle on both?
Both is okay since we've got to live with the callback form internally, it shouldn't be a major maintenance burden.

review_comments: Should there be a round trip test here? i.e. confirm that you can recreate an equivalent key by using EVP_PKEY_fromdata() on the returned params?
